answer: TripsLayerOp inputs (field: default): data: none; visible: true; opacity: 1; getPath: accessor (d) => d?.path || []; getTimestamps: accessor (d) => d?.timestamps || []; getColor: '#bfcae3'; getWidth: 8; billboard: false; capRounded: true; jointRounded: true; currentTime: 0; fadeTrail: false; trailLength: 120; widthUnits: 'meters'; widthMinPixels: 2; widthScale: 20; parameters: { depthTest: true }; extensions: empty list.
ScatterplotLayerOp's getRadius default is 20.
ScatterplotLayerOp's radiusUnits default is 'pixels'.
radiusUnits accepts 'pixels' and 'meters'.
ScatterplotLayerOp's output field is named 'layer'.
FileOp's format accepts 'json', 'csv', 'tsv', 'text', and 'binary'.
FileOp's format default is 'json'.
AccessorOp's input field is 'expression' and its output field is 'accessor'.
MaplibreBasemapOp's output field is named 'maplibre'.
DeckRendererOp's output field is named 'vis'.
TripsLayerOp's trailLength default is 120.

MathOp's operator supports 'sqrt' (yes). It does NOT support 'atan' (the trig options are only 'sine', 'cosine', and 'tan'; the full set is add, subtract, multiply, divide, sine, cosine, tan, min, max, modulo, power, log, sqrt, round, floor, ceil, abs, rad, deg).
TripsLayerOp's widthUnits accepts 'pixels', 'meters', and 'common'.
MaplibreBasemapOp's projection accepts 'mercator' and 'globe' (default 'mercator').

Available variables in an AccessorOp expression: d (current data row/item), i (row index), data (all rows), op (function to access other operators), sequenceTime (current timeline position), frame (current frame), totalFrames (total frame count), and sequence (timeline metadata). Plus utility globals such as d3, turf, etc.

MapStyleOp was removed by schema migration 014. Migration 014's up() deletes all MapStyleOp nodes (they were pass-through nodes exposing a preset map style URL) and inlines their style URL value directly onto the connected MaplibreBasemapOp's mapStyle input, then removes the MapStyleOp's edges (defaulting to CARTO_DARK if no value was set).
Migration 006 renamed the timeline sheet ID (in timeline.sheetsById) from 'Nodes' to 'Noodles'; it did not rename any operator nodes.
Migration 008 renamed the operator type 'DateOp' to 'DateTimeOp'.
Migration 013 added time markers support: it initializes an empty 'markers' array on the timeline's Noodles sheet sequence for projects that didn't have one.
The edge id is `${source}.${sourceHandle}->${target}.${targetHandle}`, e.g. '/add-1.out.result->/viewer.par.data' (source node id + '.' + sourceHandle + '->' + target node id + '.' + targetHandle).
Input (target) handles carry the 'par.' prefix (e.g. 'par.data').
Output (source) handles carry the 'out.' prefix (e.g. 'out.result').

The current schema version (NOODLES_VERSION in migrate-schema.ts) is computed as the highest migration number, which is 14. (Note: AGENTS.md documentation still states version 6, but the code's authoritative value is 14.)
The '@/' prefix (projectScheme in filesystem.ts) means the path is relative to the project's data directory; such URLs are resolved against that data directory's assets.
Node ids are Unix-style fully-qualified paths, starting with '/' for root-level operators (e.g. '/data-loader') and using '/' separators for nesting inside containers (e.g. '/container/child').
op('/data-loader').out.data

op('./sibling') resolves to an operator with the same parent container as the current operator (i.e., a sibling in the same container); resolvePath resolves relative paths against the parent path of the current operator.
A nested operator is addressed by appending its name to the container's path, e.g. '/analysis/filter' (the operator 'filter' inside container '/analysis').

A single (non-list) input accepts only one connection at a time; connecting a new edge to an occupied input replaces the existing one. The exception is ListField inputs, which accept multiple connections.
